name: Place du 16 Août
hero_subtitle: Oujda’s central square: art-deco clock tower, cafés and the everyday pulse of the city.

overview.title: The Beating Heart of Modern Oujda
overview.p1: Place du 16 Août is the main public square of Oujda. Dominated by a 1920s art-deco clock tower, it is where locals meet, sit on café terraces and watch the city go by. The square sits at the junction of the historic medina and the colonial-era boulevards.
overview.p2: Come in the late afternoon when the light softens and the terraces fill up. Order a mint tea or strong coffee and simply observe. It is one of the easiest and most pleasant ways to feel the rhythm of the Oriental capital.
overview.p3: The clock tower itself is the city’s most recognisable modern landmark. Around it you will find banks, administrative buildings and a constant flow of pedestrians and petit taxis.

1.title: Quiet and Practical
1.desc: Fewer people, good light for photos of the tower, and a calm start before exploring the medina.

2.title: Best Atmosphere
2.desc: Terraces fill, the light turns golden and the square becomes the social heart of the city.

3.title: Lights and Conversation
3.desc: After dark the square stays lively with families and groups. Ideal for a final tea before dinner.

food.title: What to Eat & Drink on the Square
food.p1: The square is lined with cafés rather than restaurants. It is the perfect place for a drink and a break.
food.li1: Mint tea or strong Moroccan coffee on a terrace.
food.li3: Simple pastries and snacks from nearby bakeries.
food.li4: For a proper meal, walk a few minutes toward the medina or the main avenues.
food.li5: Karan and barida are available in the surrounding streets.
food.p2: Prices are standard city-centre rates. Sit, order and enjoy the view – that is the point.

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Almost every petit taxi driver knows Place du 16 Août. It is also an easy walking destination from most central hotels.

2.title: Photos
2.desc: The clock tower is photogenic from several angles. Early morning or late afternoon give the best light.

3.title: Safety
3.desc: The square is busy and well-frequented until late. Standard city precautions apply.

q1.question: Is Place du 16 Août free to visit?
q1.answer: Yes. It is a public square open at all times. You only pay for what you order on the café terraces.

q2.question: What is the best time to go?
q2.answer: Late afternoon into the evening, when the terraces fill and the atmosphere is most lively.

q3.question: How long should I spend there?
q3.answer: 30 to 60 minutes is enough for photos and a drink. Longer if you simply want to sit and watch.

q4.question: Is it safe at night?
q4.answer: Yes. The square remains busy and well-lit. As in any city centre, keep an eye on belongings.

q5.question: Can I combine it with the medina?
q5.answer: Easily. The main medina gates are only a short walk away.
